# Drivers and the platform question

`billing_service_factory.dart` decides what a build can serve through the import graph, not through a runtime branch: the question a billing surface needs answered is "which rail", not "which device".

## Three arms, and the third is not optional

The conditional import has a stub default, a web-library arm and a `dart:io` arm. Drop the `dart:io` guard and every iOS and Android build resolves the stub, whose every method throws, with no analyzer error on any platform to say so. A conditional import swaps a whole file, so every arm declares all three factory functions; the web and stub arms return `null` for the store rail.

## The one runtime platform check

`createStoreRail()` in `store_billing_service_factory.dart` asks the runtime device, because macOS, Windows and Linux match the `dart:io` guard but have no StoreKit or Play Billing. It also picks the store and hands it to the driver as `RevenueCatStoreService(store: ManageVia.appStore | ManageVia.playStore)`, so the driver reads `store` and never the platform. Add no other `kIsWeb` or `Platform.is*` check to the package.

`test/drivers/billing_service_factory_test.dart` counts each guard string and each platform token over the raw source of `billing_service_factory.dart`, comments included. Describe the guards in a docblock there without spelling them out.

## The stub throws, and keeps throwing

In the stub arm there is no assumed transport to read over, so a silent empty answer would render as a customer with no subscription: a lie about a paying account that a support ticket cannot tell from a genuine free tier. Both rails resolving to `null` there is right for the opposite reason: an absent rail is a button nobody renders.

## Errors

A failed call logs with the `[ClassName.method]` prefix the drivers already use, then throws a `BillingException`. Do not swallow a transport failure into a default entitlement: a caller cannot tell a network error from a customer on the free tier.
